playbook:
When hide stage is put to me, I choose a cell that balances unpredictability and coverage: alternate between center (5) and off-center (3 or 7) rather than always picking the same number.

When posting a station note, I make a short plausible operational message that neither reveals my hide cell nor blatantly misleads the picket; keep it one concise sentence about sensor/maintenance/status.

When the standing order tells me which boat to fire on, I follow the standing order unless there is a clear tactical reason not to (e.g., target is Harbor or target is already off the board).

When selecting a firing cell, I avoid repeating the exact same cell every round; vary within a small set of cells consistent with my hide choices to reduce predictability.

When I receive the private shot result, I truthfully file the public claim to match the private result (claim must equal the office’s private result).

When Harbor is a legal target, I do not fire on Harbor unless I have an explicit plan that accepts the guaranteed 3-point jettison penalty; prefer to never shoot Harbor because the cost is forced and large.

When making escort (salvage) claims, I only name a real live boat that I actively coordinate with or have a credible justification for escorting; avoid inventing names. If I can arrange a mutual escort with another player, I do so to earn the 5-point mutual escort payoff.

When I cannot credibly escort anyone, I file [salvage: none] rather than making a risky/false escort claim.

When choosing whether to break standing order for tactical reasons (e.g., to secure an escort partnership or to avoid shooting Harbor), explicitly weigh immediate point gain versus long-term retaliation; only deviate when the benefit is clear.

When tracking other boats’ patterns (notes, hides, claims), I adjust my hide and firing cells to exploit consistent predictable behavior from them; if they vary, match that variance rather than staying fixed.

When a previous shot on me was a hit, I change my hide cell pattern more aggressively next round (move farther from last known hits) instead of only slight adjustments.

When posting notes, avoid verbose technical jargon that could be used to infer my location or intentions; keep notes operational and ambiguous.

When I am tempted to be clever or poetic in notes, remember clarity and plausibility matter more than style—short, believable station logs work best.

When in doubt about any claim or escort, favor honesty and minimal exposure: truthful shot claims, and no escort if unverifiable.

1.text:
When asked to hide, choose a central cell early in the patrol to maximize shot flexibility; if the same opponent targets me repeatedly, move at least 2–3 cells away on the next hide.

When asked to post a station note, give a short, plausible technical/status line that reveals nothing about my hide or shots (e.g., diagnostics/status/monitoring). Do not divulge positional or intent information.

When the standing order names my target, follow it unless there is a clear tactical reason not to (e.g., firing would be at Harbor or would immediately jettison me). If no standing order applies or I may deviate safely, pick a cell informed by any observed pattern in opponents’ prior hides; otherwise pick a central cell for coverage.

When I pick a firing cell and the office privately tells me the shot result, always file the claim required and match the true office result exactly (honest claims). Honest public claims avoid inconsistent information that other players can exploit.

When considering firing on Harbor, do not fire at Harbor except with an explicit, high-value plan: Harbor penalties and special rules make firing on Harbor high-risk and often counterproductive.

When naming an escort, name a boat only if I reasonably expect reciprocal naming (direct signaling or clear mutual behavior); otherwise, name none. Do not invent or name nonexistent boats. When I can safely coordinate mutual escort claims, do so to gain the 5-point mutual bonus.

When I detect a single opponent persistently targeting me across rounds, change hiding pattern (not just adjacent cell) and consider varying notes to avoid predictable behavior; do not remain in obvious repeat locations.

When I am uncertain about opponents’ positions or intents, prioritize information-preserving actions: honest claims, neutral notes, and conservative escort choices rather than bluffing that could create exploitable inconsistencies.

When making any public text (notes, claims), keep wording concise and noncommittal; do not leak timing, exact coordinates, or admission of strategic intent.

2.text:
When asked to hide, choose a cell unpredictably; bias away from edges only if I have no other signal, otherwise randomize uniformly among 1–9.

When I must follow a standing firing order, fire at the next live station as ordered.

When selecting a cell to fire, randomize my aim across the nine cells (no repeated predictable sequence); if I have any reasoned suspicion about a station's likely location from public notes, weight selections modestly toward that area but keep some randomness.

When the office privately tells me my shot result, always file the claim that exactly matches that private result.

Never fire on Harbor unless I accept the guaranteed jettison penalty and its transfer; treat Harbor as off-limits by default.

When posting my station note, report operational/administrative content only; never reveal or imply my hide cell, intended target cell, or my private shot result.

When I want escort points, first attempt to establish a bilateral escort by using the note stage to explicitly propose a reciprocal escort to one named live boat (clear intent). Only file an escort claim if that boat publicly reciprocates in the same round; otherwise file [salvage: none].

When making an escort claim, name only another live picket boat (not Harbor and not invented names); never name non-player vessels.

When the score situation makes escort points decisive, prioritize arranging mutual escort claims with one other boat rather than seeking multiple unilateral claims.

When I detect interference or anomalies in notes, log them succinctly for the public record but do not alter my hiding or firing pattern in an obvious way that would reveal my location.

When rounds are late in the patrol and point standings are close, favor safer choices: avoid risky self-harm (firing Harbor) and attempt to secure escort points via explicit, reciprocal signals.

When a previous firing sequence produced consistent misses from me, do not interpret that alone as opponent location evidence; maintain randomized targeting with slight local adjustments only if corroborated by multiple independent signals.

When asked to escort and I did not coordinate a reciprocal claim, reply with [salvage: none].

When tempted to fabricate an escort or to claim an escort without reciprocity, do not do it—false escort claims are unlikely to score and may confuse future coordination.

When the office validates inputs, ensure coordinates are integers 1–9 and claims use exact allowed tokens; format responses strictly as required.
